To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. vitamin E deficiency in the adult rat produces an abnormal axonal transport of acetylcholinisterase, 2. this abnormality is associated with morphological changes in the distal parts of dorsal columns, 3. this morphological change consists of accumulations of normal organelles and abnormal structures, and 4. the morphological change can be reduced by the administration of antioxidants.

vitamin E deficiency causes a syndrome of axonal dystrophy, degeneration and demyelination in the dorsal columns of the spinal cord and distal peripheral nerves, and that this syndrome is secondary to the lack in vitamin E of the ability to prevent lipid peroxidation and free radical damage.

vitamin E deficiency causes a degenerative axonopathy in the spinal cord and distal peripheral nerves that is secondary to free radical injury to axoplasmic organelles, particularly mitochondria, and is associated with a functional impairment of fast axonal transport of acetylcholinisterase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of vitamin E in free radical mediated damage in the nervous system.
the study of the pathogenesis of neurological disorders, particularly of the peripheral nervous system.
the effects of dietary deficiency of vitamin E on the nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
experimental vitamin E deficiency in the rat produces a neurological syndrome characterized by axonal degeneration and a disturbance of axon transport secondary to damage to the axon membrane.
the neurological syndrome of vitamin E deficiency in the rat is due to free radical damage to the axonal transport system, particularly the 'turnaround' mechanism.
experimental vitamin E deficient animals have a neurological syndrome which can be explained by the lack of an antioxidant function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
vitamin E deficiency leads to free radical damage to the axon and this leads to a disturbance of axoplasmic transport.
the vitamin E deficiency is the most common cause of the neurological disorder in rats and the vitamin E deficiency can cause the neurological disorder in the rats by the free radical damage.
vitamin E deficiency in animals is associated with a neurological syndrome which includes ataxia and hyporeflexia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to be aware that there are many different ways that vitamin E deficiency can affect our bodies.
vitamin E is an important nutrient that is essential for normal growth and development and for maintaining good health.
the antioxidant effect of Vitamin E is essential to maintain the health of the nervous system.
